title_suffix: bounded native waits and stable task-review freshness
summary: OSpec 1.8.5 fixes Goal controllers that could appear frozen for hours while a native child or review wait blocked the active model session. Every native adapter, including Codex/GPT and Claude, now publishes a bounded polling, heartbeat, incremental-result, and re-tick contract. Task reviews no longer repeat solely because unrelated commits moved Git HEAD, while final review remains strictly bound to both its target snapshot and HEAD. Unknown native capacity conservatively limits implementation batches without serializing independent reviews, and new broad task boundaries require an explicit scope reason.
new: Added machine-readable native wait fields for a 30-second polling cadence, 60-second maximum wait, heartbeat-before-due, incremental result persistence, and re-tick behavior across every registered native harness.
Added heartbeatDueAt directly to emitted action items so controllers can schedule the first lease refresh without reconstructing pending state.
Added scope_reason to 1.8.5 task graphs; tasks with more than six target files must be split or explain one atomic bounded ownership boundary.
improved: Unknown-capacity native harnesses now emit at most two implementation actions while retaining configured parallel task-review execution; reported harness capacity remains authoritative.

Controller prompts and the packaged Codex Goal skill now require bounded wait_agent or native polling, per-child heartbeat refresh, immediate sibling result persistence, and a new Loop tick after every poll.
fixed: Fixed task reviews being invalidated and re-dispatched when Git HEAD changed but every reviewed target file remained byte-for-byte unchanged.
Fixed native controller guidance allowing one indefinite Claude Task, Codex wait_agent, or other harness wait to prevent Loop observation, heartbeat renewal, and progress for hours.
Fixed final-review documentation incorrectly claiming that BLOCKED creates grouped repair; BLOCKED remains a blocker-resolution gate and only NEEDS_CHANGES creates a repair wave.
docs: Documented the 1.8.5 review freshness split, cross-harness bounded execution contract, unknown-capacity implementation guard, broad-task scope requirement, and corrected final-review behavior.
